svg.title: RIEMANN F1 — What the stages pass to each other: the 24 definitions of the blueprint, how they are built from one another, and which chapters use each
svg.desc: Every other poster follows the theorems. This one follows the definitions: the objects one chapter of the proof makes and another consumes. Each card is one of the blueprint's definitions, with the Lean declaration it stands for, the definition in words, and the chapter that makes it in its pill. Read the grid from the foot up: a definition stands above the definitions stated in terms of it, and an arrow from A to B says that B is defined using A. The table at the foot is the flow between stages: for each definition, how many statements of each chapter use it, with the chapter that makes it marked. The outline's own section on the interfaces names three definitions as what the arithmetic stages pass to the analytic ones; those three are used by 35 statements in 7 chapters. No Lean was built: see diagram R1, band 5.

A → B: definition B is stated in terms of A (the arrow takes A's colour)

Title and pill. The title is the blueprint's; the pill gives the kind, the chapter that makes the definition, and the provenance: new in Alpöge's proof, modified from a published definition, or published as it
stands. Definitions are drawn with a dashed border on every poster of this set.

The Lean panel is the signature of the first declaration the blueprint lists for the definition, as lean-facts.json records it, wrapped and cut at nine lines. The footer gives its file and line in the mirror and the
The line in italics is the blueprint's definition, abridged where marked with …; links appear as ids and maths is rewritten in plain Unicode. A definition has no proof, so there are no bullets.

Stated with and Used by are the blueprint's edges. Used in counts the statements of each chapter that use the definition, in their statement or their proof; it is the row of the table at the foot. Rows: a card
stands above the definitions stated in terms of it; cards of one chapter sit together where the arrows allow.

text.tspan: The interfaces, in the outline's own words (

svg.text: Three statements pass from the arithmetic stages to the analytic ones, and several chapters use each. A system of local parameters (def-local-parameters) is a weak form of the local Langlands
correspondence for GL_n, and a direct construction shows that one exists (thm-local-parameters-exist). Galois representations of polarized pairs (def-galois-reps-polarized) are compatible with
such a system; chap-galois proves that they exist. The Tate–Shafarevich bound (def-sha-bound) bounds the lengths of Ш^1 over the ψ-fields of a 2-power cyclotomic tower; chap-sha proves it with
The three def-local-parameters (made in Outline, used by 25 statements), def-galois-reps-polarized (made in Outline, used by 5 statements), def-sha-bound (made in Outline, used by 5
Made 24 definitions: 3 in Main theorems, 3 in Outline, 5 in Zero-free, 7 in Families, 3 in Theta,
2 in Sha, 1 in Literature. By provenance: 4 modified, 14 new, 5 published, 1 unlabelled.
Built from one another 10 of them are stated in terms of another definition; the 18 arrows of
the grid. The tallest tower is the families chapter's, from auxiliary field data up to family data.
Consumed Main theorems 5, Outline 16, Zero-free 21, Families 27, Theta 9, Heights 2, Sha
9, Galois 5, Literature 3 statements use a definition. Used most def-local-parameters

The Riemann Hypothesis is the statement that every zero s of the Riemann zeta function other
than the trivial zeros -2, -4, -6, … satisfies Re s = 1/2. Here ζ is defined on all of ℂ and
given an arbitrary value at its pole s = 1, so the statement also excludes s = 1.

text.tspan: Non-vanishing right of the critical line

svg.text: ∀ (N : ℕ) [NeZero N] (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ N) (s : ℂ), 1 / 2
We say that Dirichlet L-functions do not vanish right of the critical line if for every modulus N ≥
1, every Dirichlet character χ modulo N, primitive or not, and every s with Re s > 1/2, L(χ,
s) ≠ 0, the pole χ = 1, s = 1 excepted.
Used in 7 statements in 2 chapters: Outline 5, Main theorems 2

Let E/F be a CM extension and fix rank data (k, m, t) (def-family-ranks). A hermitian
space here is a finite-dimensional E-vector space V with a nondegenerate hermitian form, a
basis, its signature at each embedding E → ℂ, and a unimodular mathcal O_E-lattice L_0 ⊂ V.

text.tspan: Zeros in the critical strip lie on the line

svg.text: ∀ (N : ℕ) [NeZero N] (χ : DirichletCharacter ℂ N) (s : ℂ),
We say that the zeros of Dirichlet L-functions in the critical strip lie on the line if for every
modulus N ≥ 1 and every Dirichlet character χ modulo N, every zero of L(χ, s) with 0 < Re
s < 1 has Re s = 1/2. We use the same phrase restricted to primitive characters.

svg.text: ∀ (la : ℝ) (G : FReq), 1 < la → HostExW la G.req →

We say that families have slope data if, for every λ > 1 and every requirement on auxiliary
fields, the following holds. Suppose fields meeting the requirement exist on windows [Y, Y^λ],
and the members of every family(@def-family) in the corresponding class eventually satisfy
the Tate–Shafarevich bound. Then for some constants e_D, e_L and every small ε, some
family in the class carries slope data (def-slope-data) at every large x of its windows.
